effect_size.excerpt: After adjusting confounding factors, it was observed that the odds of bladder cancer were significantly lower in the second and last tertiles (T) of total peptide intake from dairy products compared to the first tertile (T 2 : odds ratio (OR) = 0.285; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.116–0.699, T 3 : OR = 0.130; 95% CI: 0.032–0.527). headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 6 studies yielded an effect size of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.54–1.13), indicating no statistically significant association between dairy and bladder cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 81.22%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
